clue.text: Vault over piece of wood close to gangway cracking craft

parts.note: a vault under a church is a crypt
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
a log is a piece of wood

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of gangway

explanation.surface: An acrobat leaps a plank lying near a ship's gangway as part of some practical skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a verb for jumping, but it is the noun: an underground chamber. 'cracking craft' means the craft of cracking codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptology is the science of making and breaking codes, a skill whose aim is code-cracking.

clue.text: Put one's hands together for hit band

definitions.meaning: to handcuff someone is to fasten their hands together
to strike someone lightly with the open hand
the band of material at the end of a sleeve

explanation.surface: An audience is asked to applaud a successful pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's hands together' looks like clapping, but it means fastening someone's wrists. 'hit band' looks like a chart-topping group, but it is two more senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuff as verb means both to handcuff and to slap; as a noun it is a sleeve's end band.

clue.text: Return fixture football team to play at last, no matter what

indicators.note: return means the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a fixture in sport is a tie, a scheduled match
Man U is the usual short name for Manchester United

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the words to and play

explanation.surface: A return match against a football side is due to be played, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns everything: TIE, MANU and OY (the last letters of 'to' and 'play') run backwards give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said after a list to mean anything at all, whatever you like, no matter what.

clue.text: Wells work daily, bottomless pit outside a church

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, which is removed

parts.note: The Times is a daily newspaper

indicators.note: the mine goes outside, around, the following pieces

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a deep pit lies beside a church in Wells, the cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' looks like the Somerset city but is H. G. Wells. 'bottomless' drops the S of THE TIMES, leaving THE TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: H. G. Wells wrote the 1895 novel about time travel, so it is a work by him.

clue.text: Spotted small flier being lifted by lawyer in drag

indicators.note: in places the lifted pair inside the word for drag

parts.note: to lug something is to drag it

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the letters read upwards, so in reverse

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A tiny insect is picked up by a lawyer dressed in women's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drag' suggests cross-dressing, but drag is just the verb to haul; 'being lifted' turns BY plus DA upwards to ADYB.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybug, the American name for a ladybird, is a small flying beetle with spots.

clue.text: It may be sucked down beneath cement

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means this piece follows the other

parts.note: gum is a glue or cement
to drop is to go down

explanation.surface: Something lies underneath a layer of cement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy sweet, which is eaten by sucking or chewing it.

clue.text: Spade for one burying clubs and racket

indicators.note: burying means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Sam Spade is the private eye in The Maltese Falcon
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A garden spade buries some golf clubs amid a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spade' looks like a digging tool or the card suit, but it is Dashiell Hammett's detective Sam Spade.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket in slang is a dishonest scheme for making money, the same as a con.

clue.text: Variety of rose bud

definitions.meaning: the ... rose is a garden rose from East Asia
bud is American slang for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A gardener talks of a rosebud of a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bud' looks like part of the rose, but it means a pal: CHINA means mate from Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the name of a rose group and, through rhyming slang, a word for a friend.

clue.text: Endless fat sandwiches in a row, soaking

indicators.note: sandwiches means one piece encloses the others like bread around a filling
endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: marge, short for margarine, is a cooking fat
a row, a loud noise, is a din

explanation.surface: Fat is endlessly spread in sandwiches laid out in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts MARGE to MARG, and 'sandwiches' puts INADIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marinading meat is steeping it in a seasoned liquid, so it is soaking.

clue.text: Prodigious drinker smothering duff in jam

parts.note: a bumper crop is a huge one, so bumper means prodigious

indicators.note: smothering means one piece covers the other, taking it inside

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
bum and duff both mean poor quality, worthless

explanation.surface: A huge drinker is stuck in some jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like fruit preserve, but it is a traffic jam.
explanation.definitionFit: In a traffic jam cars queue with almost no gap, each nose close to the car in front.

clue.text: One lucky having fine physician as bookmaker

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
St Luke was a physician and wrote a Gospel, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A lucky gambler with a good doctor who also takes bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' looks like a turf accountant, but here it is a writer of a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke is a lucky chance or stroke, a success owed to luck rather than skill.

clue.text: Writer injecting element of great value into one murder novel

indicators.note: injecting means one piece is inserted into the other
into means the numeral for one goes inside the rearranged murder
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A writer adds something precious to a murder mystery novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being written, but it means new, signalling a rearrangement (to DUMRER); 'into' and 'injecting' each place one piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier was the English novelist who wrote Rebecca and Jamaica Inn.

clue.text: Training ground gets old Premier League leader in trouble

parts.note: Lord Salisbury was a Victorian Prime Minister

indicators.note: in means the leader is placed inside the trouble

parts.note: a pain is a trouble or nuisance

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of League

explanation.surface: A former Premier League top scorer finds himself in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier League' looks like English football's top division, but it splits: an old Prime Minister, then the leader of League. SALISBURY PLAIN in Wiltshire is a large army training area.
explanation.definitionFit: This Wiltshire plateau is the British Army's chief training area, a ground for exercises.

clue.text: Wheels on firm ground ram bottom of plastic canopy

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged
in a down clue the bottom is the last letter of plastic

explanation.surface: On solid ground a ram butts the base of a plastic awning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is slang for a car, so the definition means a car provided by an employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels is slang for a car, and one supplied by an employer is a firm's vehicle.

clue.text: Something to do with pudding topping, say: last of icing

parts.note: a topping is something over the top of something else
eg, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of icing

explanation.surface: Something about a dessert's topping, perhaps the final bit of icing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is to over-egg the pudding, so this verb is what one does to a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom over-egg the pudding means overdo it, so the verb is linked with pudding.

clue.text: Combustible heap almost in centre of old monument

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning
amid means in the middle of

explanation.surface: A heap that will burn lies near the middle of an ancient monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PYRE to PYR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian pyramids are ancient royal tombs, among the most famous old monuments.

clue.text: Cold and coming down outside, most important to button it!

definitions.text: Cold and coming down outside, most important to button it!

indicators.note: outside means the main piece goes round the cold letter

parts.note: main means chief, most important
C is the tap abbreviation for cold
button it means shut up, which is sh

explanation.surface: Advice for cold rainy weather: the vital thing is to button up your coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes when to wear and button a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a waterproof raincoat, worn when it is cold and raining outdoors.

clue.text: They'd cut a deal: it's in exchange for backing

indicators.note: in means it's goes inside the reversed exchange
backing means the word for exchange is read backwards

parts.note: to swap is to exchange

explanation.surface: Terms of a business deal: something is traded in return for support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut a deal' looks like making an agreement, but deal is timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit saws are long two-man saws used to cut timber, and deal is pine or fir wood.

clue.text: Sort of protest rulers and numerous other leaders voice

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A kind of protest by rulers and many other leaders makes itself heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest singing voice, and a singer with one.

clue.text: Card game my granny passes about

parts.note: coo and my are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: passes means the granny goes round the other piece

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
C is the abbreviation of circa, about

explanation.surface: An old woman passes around cards in a game, to an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation, like 'goodness'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coon can is a rummy-type card game, an ancestor of gin rummy.

clue.text: One making cold call, having zero information

parts.note: to cry is to call out
O looks like zero
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A telemarketer making a cold call has nothing to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold call' looks like a sales phone call, but the definition stops at 'cold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryogen is a substance such as liquid nitrogen used to produce very low temperatures.

clue.text: Cross, by pony, path a nun travels

indicators.note: travels means the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun rides a pony along a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a crucifix suiting a nun, but it is the adjective, meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: This colloquial phrase describes someone displeased or annoyed, which is what cross means.

clue.text: Writer Kipling denied ever meeting

definitions.meaning: Kipling wrote that East and West, the two, shall never meet

explanation.surface: A writer says Kipling denied they had ever met.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's line 'never the twain shall meet' uses the old word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an old word for two, and Mark Twain was the American novelist.

clue.text: Report making little splash quietly cut

parts.note: P is the music abbreviation for piano, quietly
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A news report makes little impact, being quietly dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a news item, but it is a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plop is the soft sound made when something small drops into water.

clue.text: Labour Party unlikely to split?

parts.note: a group of convicts doing hard labour, chained together so they cannot separate

explanation.surface: A political party looks unlikely to divide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour Party' looks like the British political party, but it is a party, a group, doing labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Convicts on a chain gang are linked by a chain while working, so they cannot part.

clue.text: Steal part of wall, taking odd sections

indicators.note: taking odd sections picks the first, third, fifth and so on letters

explanation.surface: A burglar removes some of a wall, taking unusual pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' is the verb to move stealthily, not to rob.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move about stealthily, and steal can mean to creep quietly.

clue.text: One due a letter from Split

definitions.meaning: a letter is one who lets property, and the money owed to a landlord is this
a split or tear in cloth

explanation.surface: Someone is owed a letter from Split, the Croatian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence, but it means someone who lets out property.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is the payment owed to a landlord, and also a tear or split in fabric.

clue.text: Grocer's combining kicks and hard work

parts.note: corners are corner kicks in football
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A grocer's business combines football kicks and hard graft.
explanation.walkthrough: A CORNER SHOP is a small local British grocery.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner shop is a small neighbourhood store selling groceries, so it is a grocer's.
